title: Chronic Implantation of Gastrointestinal and Vagus Nerve Electrodes in Ferrets
author: Charles C Horn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6crhav6
materials: Make dorsal midline incision on the head.
Clear muscle tissue from dorsal skull.
Monitor animal for recovery from isoflurane.
Shave abdomen and dorsal neck and head.
Intubate using a 3.0 or 3.5 endotracheal tube.

steps.title: Pre-operative Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for surgery by managing diet and monitoring vitals.

substeps.instruction: Remove food from the home cage 3 hours before anesthesia.
Measure body weight.
Apply facemask to deliver inhalational isoflurane (1 to 2%).
Place ferret supine on table.
Connect EKG leads and place rectal probe to maintain body temperature between 36 to 40C.
Sterilize skin for incision with chlorohexidine and 70% isopropyl alcohol.
Monitor vitals with pulse oximeter, EKG, and rectal temperature probe following sterile procedure.

steps.title: Initial Incisions and Tunneling
steps.instruction: Create surgical access and tunnels for electrode leads and catheters.

substeps.instruction: Make incisions in skin on the abdominal midline (~4 cm) and dorsal neck (~3 cm).
Use a trocar to tunnel under skin from the dorsal neck, along the back, and to the left side to exit at the abdominal incision.
Advance electrode leads and gastric catheter through the tunnel with the trocar, then remove the trocar.

steps.title: Abdominal Cavity Exposure
steps.instruction: Open the abdominal cavity and expose the target organs.

substeps.instruction: Place the animal on its back.

Open abdominal cavity using a 3-point retractor (Balfour pediatric retractor; George Tiemann) applied to the lateral edges of the abdominal incision and sternum, elevated using a vertical post attached to a surgical board.
Make an incision in the midline abdominal muscle to expose the organs.
Perform caudal retraction of the stomach and retraction of the liver to the right side using saline moistened gauze to make the esophagus and vagi accessible.

steps.title: Gastric Catheter and Electrode Placement
steps.instruction: Insert the gastric catheter and place electrodes on the gastrointestinal tract and vagus nerve.

substeps.instruction: Make an incision (~0.5 cm) on the left lateral edge of the gastric fundus and insert the gastric catheter with the tip resting in the antrum.
Place and tie a purse-string suture around the incision; tie an additional knot around the catheter and tie the free ends of this knot and the purse-string suture together.
Apply surgical glue (Vetbond) to the incision area.
If required, place a cuff electrode on either the ventral or dorsal abdominal vagus nerve trunk.
Place planar electrodes on the surface of the stomach and duodenum using 8-0 silk suture.
Suture a ground electrode lead to connective tissue on the greater curvature of the stomach.

steps.title: Abdominal Lavage and Closure
steps.instruction: Clean the abdominal cavity and close the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Administer abdominal lavage with antibiotic (cefalexin, 1% w/v) in saline (0.9%, 100 ml).
Test electrode impedances using a Grapevine Neural Interface Processor and a Nano2 recording headstage (Ripple LLC).
Close abdomen using absorbable suture for muscle (silk, 2-0) and monofilament (3-0) for the skin.

steps.title: Cranial Implant and Connector Fixation
steps.instruction: Secure the electrode connectors to the skull using bone cement.

substeps.instruction: Turn the animal to dorsal side up.
Fix the head in place using a stereotaxic frame and earbars.
Tunnel under the skin between the head and neck incision and pull electrode connectors through to the head.
Suture the gastric tube to the neck and close the neck incision.
Drill 4 to 8 holes in the skull and place bone screws, leaving space between the screw head and skull for bone cement grip.
Layer bone cement onto the skull to form a base.
Use bone cement to mount and surround the connectors.
Measure electrode impedances using a Grapevine Neural Interface Processor and a Nano2 recording headstage (Ripple LLC).

steps.title: Post-operative Care and Recovery
steps.instruction: Provide medication and wound care during the recovery period.

substeps.instruction: Leave ~6 cm of the leads with head connector extended from the dorsal neck incision, wrapped in sterile gauze and taped to surrounding skin.
Administer 10 days of oral amoxicillin and 72 hours of buprenorphine (s.c.).
Administer 20 ml of warm saline (s.c.) and repeat every two hours.
Remove sutures 2 weeks after surgery.
Record 10 min of baseline gastrointestinal myoelectric responses using a Grapevine Neural Interface Processor and a Nano2 recording headstage (Ripple LLC).
